physicalNotes: Radius 1.51 +/- 0.02 solar radii and temperature 3650 +/- 20 K: the SPHINX model-atmosphere fit to the pair's blended optical spectrum, modelled as the sum of the two stars by Inglis et al. (2024, AJ; doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ad2771; arXiv:2402.09533), Table 1. Their text gives 1.42 and 1.59 solar radii for the two stars instead of the table's 1.51 and 1.39; the table is used. A model radius: the disc is not measured. 1,050,507 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. GM from the photometric mass 0.89 +/- 0.08 solar masses of Kraus et al. (2014, ApJ 781, 20; arXiv:1311.7664) times the JPL solar GM. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; no spin axis is measured on the sky.

sources.position: Gaia DR3 source 6047587937321868288 (Gaia Collaboration 2023, A&A 674, A1), ICRS at epoch J2016.0. Gaia DR3 does not resolve A and B, 83 mas apart: its position, parallax and motion are the pair's photocentre (RUWE 2.1). This record places A there, and B on its measured orbit around A (Inglis et al. 2026).
sources.distance: Gaia DR3 source 6047587937321868288: parallax 6.8284 mas, inverted to 146.4464 pc with no zero-point correction.
sources.properMotion: Gaia DR3 source 6047587937321868288: pmRA* -5.7318 mas/yr, pmDec -23.3664 mas/yr.
sources.radialVelocity: Gaia DR3 source 6047587937321868288: -0.68 +/- 13.37 km/s, the pair's combined light; poorly measured (Gaia DR2 gave 1.13 +/- 7.97).
